utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. The parties will have seen the Chamber's decision to suspend the hearing of evidence for a period of two weeks following the completion of the testimony of Mr. Blaszczyk, which is likely to be the two-week period starting on Monday, 23rd of August. The parties had previously been advised that the Chamber would not sit on Wednesday, 15th, Thursday 16th, Friday 17th, Monday, 20th, and Tuesday, 21st September. However, in light of the two weeks suspension, the Chamber is minded now to sit on 15th and 16th September, although it will be unable to do so on 17th, 20th, and 21st September. We will therefore ask the registry to put us back into the court schedule on those two days. I should note that the Chamber is also contemplating holding a Status Conference during the period of the suspension to discuss the progress of the trial to date. We will advise you at the end of Mr. Blaszczyk's testimony when that will occur. That said, we will bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I address you before the witness is brought in?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He's already in, but.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's no problem. Yesterday we referred to the report of Mr. Higgs, 10083. That's the 65 ter number. We did not refer to the amalgamated statement. It was P1437 that had been prepared for another case. I say this for the sake of clarifying the transcript, so that there is no confusion in terms of what we were referring to. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Higgs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sorry for your inconvenience. There have been some matters to be dealt with in your absence. Mr. Karadzic, let's -- let's continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 65 ter number 09893. Let us see page 1 and then move on to page 10 in English and 9 in Serbian. Serbian 9, English 10. Those are the page numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: First of all, good morning to everyone, to all the participants. Now, Mr. Higgs, on the basis of all the reports available in this case and all the information submitted to you, photographs of the site and the maps of the area involved, you established the azimuth for the shell in relation to Markale II, and your report says, "I have reviewed all of these reports, and as I used the maps and the material related to this area, I was able to confirm the correct bearing by using these methods." What was the conclusion that you reached exactly after analysing these documents?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My conclusion was to agree with the initial findings, that of the bearing of 1 -- the proximate bearing of 170 degrees was far more accurate than the presumed bearing of 220 to 240 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Whose assumption was that, 220?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The figures of 220 to 240 came from a second UNPROFOR investigation carried out after the -- the initial first three done by UNPROFOR, the French, and the forensic teams.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you -- could you explain to us briefly how it was that you established that bearing? You say in your report of the 3rd of August, 2006, "First of all, I reviewed the photographs of the crater to see what was traces were and where it was in relation to the road. On the basis of the traces -- or, rather, their form, we can see roughly how the projectile fell on the road."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: We do not have the text.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the interpreters. I did not give a reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "On that basis, I was supposed to see what the relationship was between this crater and the road and to try to get a bearing from crater to road. Once I had a bearing related to the road, I could then calculate the road direction and then consequently the true bearing and the -- the true bearing that the crater is facing." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I looked at all the information from the reports I'd been given and the photographs that you mention. On looking at the photographs, then looking at the shape of the crater, the direction it was facing, towards the building, and then taking approximate bearings of in relation to the road to try and establish whether or not it is closer towards a bearing of 170 or closer to a bearing of 220 as suggested in the reports. From that, in my opinion, the crater points closer towards the bearing of 170.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have 65 ter number 09893, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is this not what we are looking at?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. We're asking for page 546 in Serbian and page 4 in English from the same document -- or, no. No. Just a moment, please. English page 4 and Serbian page 12. Basically it's page 12 of the document itself, so it's two pages further up, and in Serbian it's probably three. One more page. We're actually looking for the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us now look at this photograph in order to be clearer on this. Is this the photograph of the crater that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are this crater and photograph a bit different than we had seen? In the film I mean.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is the crater that you saw on the video that the -- the French were taking the measurements from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll have a look at the film in order to establish whether there is a difference involved. What is this 275, the figure written up there? What does that denote?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When trying to determine the approximate bearing at which the round came in, the only references you have on the photograph, of course, is the crater and the road. So by then looking at the maps to see the approximate bearing along which the road runs, that is the approximate, 275 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The azimuth, the direction of the road; right? How was it that you established this? Did you use a map, or did you apply some kind of measurement?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was taken as an approximate bearing from a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It's the same document but page 13 now. Could we have the next page, the map, to see whether it is the map that you worked with, the one that's in the report. Is that the map?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D2252. Could we have that in e-court, please. That is a detail from this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We marked certain things on your map. Is this what you established to be the 275 degrees trajectory?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 275 is represented by that line as shown on the map there. That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So was this marked properly then? Was Markale marked properly, the actual site?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The site on the maps was -- as I remember, was not marked as it is, obviously, on this one. I was working off the grid references given on the reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But it's the same map that you worked off; right? Do you recall that the explosion was to the south of the tram line? Right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that what is marked by this arrow saying "Markale Market"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tram line I -- on here I assume is being represented by the black line with the -- the cross-hatches across the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. You can see that. Right. All right. I would like to ask you if you would be so kind as to mark -- or, rather, to place the date on this map and to initial it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He didn't mark anything, so why does he have to mark it at all?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. But he identified the site of the explosion and trajectory 275. We entered the markings that are now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. Mr. Higgs, are you able to mark on this map the place where the explosion took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not just with this map, Your Honour. I would need, obviously, more information, because the precise location on the ground was never something I was ever asked to confirm, only to confirm or give my opinion on a bearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But we can notice that this is a -- this is a map which is zoomed in from the map that we had previously seen in one -- in your report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This witness, Mr. Higgs, is not sure where -- whether this -- the marked place as "Markale Market" is exactly the same place as the place where the explosion took place.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'd say I was working off the grid references that was given to me in the reports. I had no reason, obviously, to doubt where they were, and working off of the video and the photographs that I could see, and from that is where I then did my work regarding trying to identify the possible direction from which that round came.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Gaynor, would you oppose to the admission of this document with that caveat, that Markale Market is marked by the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No, I don't object. Simply to go back a few lines where Mr. Karadzic referred to the trajectory of 275, I just want it absolutely clear for the record that that is not considered by the witness to be the trajectory of the projectile. That's simply a direction of 275 degrees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it you agree, Mr. Higgs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: With that caveat, with that explanation, we'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D543, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Higgs. You worked on the basis of this map, and you established the direction of the road and the direction from which the shell came on the basis of this map; right? So there was no other map.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked on the basis of this map and the other map which is in my report. However, this one being the most detailed that I had and used this to get the approximate directions of the road, remembering, of course, that these are only approximate directions of which the road approximately runs along.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D2238, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see this map now, and can you see the localities -- or, rather, the sites where the explosions took place? You see the market area in depth. We see one explosion. It's probably Markale I. And do you see the rest? Do you agree that that is the place where the shell from Markale II exploded?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we agree, then, that you were not correct in establishing the direction of the road and that that deviation is considerable and that therefore it had to affect the establishment of the location where the mine -- or the shell fell?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said before, it was the approximate direction along the road, and as you can see if you look along the whole the road on which it faces, the road runs approximately east to west. There will always be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Higgs, to interrupt you. Although the witness was able to confirm where the Markale I or Markale II are, I'm not. Could you help the Chamber where it is marked. Could you direct where it is, with the assistance of the usher. Where's the Markale I?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. From this map here, the two rounds being referred to, would be those two there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. And where is Markale II?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, Markale II would be the second one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Second one, yes. I see. Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Higgs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I ask the witness to mark it M1 and M2.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: With a 1 and a 2?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Magic touch. And as for the provenance of this map, who marked this -- this marking, Mr. Karadzic? Is it done by your team?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we're not hearing the translation of what you said. Shall we give it another try?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a street plan of Sarajevo where sites of three explosions were marked in another case, and you can see from the number below at the bottom, 1D01, et cetera. I think it was from the Milosevic case. It's a regular street plan marked with the sites of three explosions. The first was the Miskin street, the queue for bread, the next one is Markale 1, and the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. I'm simply asking who did these markings.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that's a street plan made probably in Sarajevo. It's a regular street plan you can buy anywhere, and it's marked. We'll identify the publisher now. I believe it's a publisher from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Higgs, if you can kindly marked 1 and 2 on Markale I and Markale II.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please put the date and your initials.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, the Bosniak institute of Mr. Zulfikarpasic is the author of this map. They made the markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The numbers 1 and 2 referring to Markale, I kindly ask you to put the date below and your initials.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, we'll admit this as Exhibit D544.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I now ask for 65 ter 15061, and that would be page 9. ERN number is 0033-9206.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime while we are waiting, Mr. Gaynor, have we admitted the 65 ter number 9893, among which the map reappears? Mr. Karadzic, did you want to tender that report by Mr. Higgs into evidence, or you just used it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it's not yet an exhibit, we would like to tender it. If it's the same one we referred to, not the amalgamated one the Prosecution tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: This particular report has not yet been admitted. We have no objection to its admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll admit it as a Defence exhibit. That will be Exhibit D545.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, I ask you to tell us if this is the site of the explosion and whether you received that as part of your documentation, and can you identify the fragments, the traces in the form of beams, rays. I hope that the transcript will be corrected. Is this the photograph of the site that you were given as the site of descent of the second shell, Markale II, and which is marked. It says here that it's before the clean-up. It says: "The site of descent of the mortar projectile calibre 120 millimetres, marked number 1 before clean-up and marking." Is that it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is one of the many photographs that I was presented.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I now ask you to mark on this site the characteristic traces of the fragments of the shell on the asphalt, the centre of the explosion, the first crown, the second crown, and the ray-like traces.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not the best photograph to do that, because you do not get clear sight of the crater from this photograph, which is why I used the better quality one which looked down onto the crater.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you talking about the one that we were told was marked by chalk, because there is a reference to marking here. Were there any markings on the photograph that you studied?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this particular photograph we're now looking at here, the quality of the photograph and from where the photograph is taken, you cannot make out the pattern of the crater at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about zooming in this photo a little bit? Still it's not --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Still not the best photograph, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about the next page, or the page after -- next one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that one again is really too -- too far away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about this one? We can zoom in a bit further.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This photograph has been taken close in to mainly show the crater. It doesn't show the entire fragment pattern. This photograph concentrates on looking at the point of impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I read to you, Mr. Higgs, what it says below the photograph: "Close-up of the site of descent and explosion of the projectile -- projectile taken after clean-up and marking." Do you now accept that they did mark these -- this pattern on the asphalt by chalk?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it says obviously in the examination that they did mark it for clarity, then I would have no reason to disbelieve what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You seem to have a lot of trust in the authors of these reports, and you said yesterday that you believed them, but this is a criminal case, and I challenge their accuracy. Can you now mark on this the elements that we mentioned, the characteristic traces on the tarmac, the centre of the explosion, the first crown, the second crown, and the ray-like pattern.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this particular photograph the second crown is difficult to determine, but the point of impact as best you can see on the photograph would be in this area, with the first crown being in that area. The photograph which looks at the crater from further away can give you a better picture of where the second crown will be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But if we -- before we go any further, if you can tell us what the first crown, second crown, or third crowns are to us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When a mortar round explodes and detonates it forms a small crater. The first lip of that crater is known as the first crown, and then when the bomb explodes, the fragments and the pressure, of course, go outwards, and where the main centre of the body explosion took place and where those fragments hit the ground, they give a fan-type shape on the ground, and that centre -- measurement to the centre of that position is known as the second crown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Higgs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please put numbers there, 1 for the point of impact, the centre of the crater, and number 2 for the first crown.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark the ray-like or the fan-type pattern and tell us something about it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not all included in this picture because this is a close-up. Some of it is contained in here, but you would need the -- the photograph which shows you the whole pattern to better show the -- the second crown.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you have such a photograph? Does such a photograph exist?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The photograph that better shows it would be the one which I used my bearings from, the one that looked down -- looks down upon it. But I did not use the first or second crowns as part of my investigation because they require calculations, and of course I had no access to the crater to carry out those calculations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, how did you then decide? What did you use to make your findings?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the findings or bearing it was the pattern, the overall pattern of the crater and the direction which it points which gives you bearing. First and second crowns come into play when, if you do not have a quality fuse furrow for calculating angle of descent, you can by ballistic calculation use the distances the first and second crowns to come up with a ballistic estimate of the angle of descent, and this is shown in the forensic report as this is one of the methods that they used.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, it might be easier if we move back -- I don't want to interfere with Mr. Karadzic's cross-examination, but there is a photograph describing exactly what the witness is referring to at page 4 of this collection of photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll do so after keeping -- after doing the housekeeping matters. So would you like to tender this document parked by Mr. Higgs?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. If he can put the date and his initials.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You want to say that there is no fuse furrow on this one?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That picture does not show any distinctive fuse furrow at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we can admit this and then move on to page 4, suggested kindly by the witness [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will admit this as Exhibit D546, and I for the record, I note this is a picture marked from the -- from page 15 of Exhibit P1448. Now we'll back to page 4 of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a correction on the record. I said it was kindly suggested by Mr. Gaynor, not the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you notice here those markings in chalk, Mr. Higgs?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the markings on the ground, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us on the basis of this photograph how you determined the direction?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On looking at this overall crater, from the shape of the crater and where the -- the majority of the shrapnel marks are in the tarmac, it is possible to come to the conclusion that from the point of impact the majority of the fragment marks are then between the point of impact on the curb facing towards the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That was enough to you to determine the angle of descent, the direction from which the shell came.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: By examining the fragments and the overall pattern, that was enough to give me an approximate bearing from which this round came, which is pointing toward the building. If this round had come from 220 to 240 as suggested in the second report, the majority of the fragments would have been pointing in this picture to the right, down the road, because that is the -- the other direction. And you can see from this picture that is not the case, that from the point of impact the majority of fragments face towards the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please draw two lines here, one showing the direction from which the round came and the second line marking the direction of 275 that you used as orientation.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bearing of 170 is approximately in that direction, and 275 approximately in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you show us the axis that coincides with the direction from which the round came, and second, across the whole photograph will you please draw the line that marks 275 degrees.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could please just confirm the question. I have just marked the line that is approximately 275, which is the one to the right. What axis would you like me to draw?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well across these traces draw us an axis that shows the direction of descent across the traces. If that's the direction you already marked, you can just stretch it to -- to cover the whole photograph. Or would you change something?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously from working from this photograph I'm obviously estimating, but the arrow to the right is approximately 275. The arrow I have drawn from the crater to the building again is approximately 170, that sort of area. The way in which I come to these findings is by looking, as I said before, the overall shape of the crater. Would it help if I was to show the pattern of the mortar round to explain that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No. Just mark this direction as 275 and the other one as 175, which you believe to be the direction from which the round came.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can this line be lengthened to show us the axis of descent, the axis of the pattern relative to the direction from which the shell came?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaze.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I just want to clarify for the record where Mr. Karadzic said, "The other one was 175, which you believe to be the direction from which the round came." It might have been a slip of the tongue by Mr. Karadzic. The witness said 170.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I think it's clear from the record. And would you like the witness to extend the other line as well?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That wouldn't be necessary if we agreed that the edge of the pavement coincides with the line 275. I don't think my question was recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Higgs, that the line of the payment coincides with the direction 275?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I have to speak fast, so not everything is recorded by -- I'm working against the clock. Can you put the date and your initials, please.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be admitted as Exhibit D547.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now get back the first map of the city, the street plan on the basis of which you marked. 1D2252. The one we marked. D543. Can we get that? D543, recently admitted. Let's just look at it briefly. It's the detail of the street plan used by Mr. Higgs. It's easier 1D2252.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Higgs, that this is not very well drawn, namely the direction 275 does not really coincide. It actually coincides more with the Mustafa Baseskija Street.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, because at the time I only had this one particular map, so I took an approximate line which represented a direction as much as possible with the roads. Obviously, I had no means of an accurate bearing. So that -- that is where the 275 came from. I was trying to use a direction which was then a -- if you like, a stable or a current connection which I could then use to work from. If -- as you can see from this blown-up picture here that the roads running around the front are the marked Markale Market is at -- could be, as you suggest, a slightly smaller bearing. It could be, if you measure this accurately, probably nearer 260 or 265. If that is the case, then that just goes to reinforce the decision the initial teams came to about the direction being 170 and not 220, 240, because the more that road has a smaller direction, i.e., less than 275, then the crater would be more facing down the road. It would be really prominent that it has come from down the road. So I use a direction of 275 of a central correction not having, as I say, any direct or detailed information. So from that I could then just look at the evidence I was given, i.e., the photographs, and then come up with my opinion of whether it came from over the building or whether it did come from down the road direction, which would have been the 220, 240. So I think this picture just goes to reinforce my opinion that the round came from a direction a lot closer than 170 and is nowhere near a direction of 220 to 240.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The line on this map, Mr. Higgs, which purports to be the line pointing to the direction 275 degrees is the correct one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is -- the line is 275 degrees. Yes, it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: On this map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. P1450. Could we have that now. Could we just see briefly what this crater looks like at the moment when the French team started working there. It's in Sanction, rather. I think that the reference is 625 or something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it's 65 ter number 40221.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I believe that the arrival of the French investigation team is at 6:51 or 6:15. Could someone help. A bit further back. Could you rewind a bit more, the moment when they're actually arriving. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the point of impact of the shell?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We are now at 5 minutes, 32 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, when was it that the French arrived?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information on timings and when people actually arrived by time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were they the first investigation group to arrive?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I don't have that information, whether they were the first or worked with any of the other teams.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this site differ from all the other photographs that we saw from the report of the Sarajevo security centre?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure on the question. In what way do you mean differ?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, first of all, this is not soaked in blood. Also, the form and depth of this crater looks different, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is obviously the video. It does not show the whole area. And as you made the point on the previous photographs, the photographs were taken, as you said, after clean-up, which of course would have moved blood around on the scene when they did it and given a different picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How do you explain those photographs where the crater is full of blood? How come? Where was the point of impact of the shell? Did the shell hit a human being or the asphalt?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no evidence that the round on it's path down hit a human being. You can see, although this picture is not the best, that the round has struck the ground. Obviously the blood all around came from the casualties which would have been in that vicinity. The differences between the video and the still shots I can only assume is that, as you made the point earlier, some of the still shots were taken after some form of clean-up had taken place, and therefore it could have spread, obviously, the blood patterns all around.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This has already been admitted, and we don't need it any longer. Otherwise, this footage is going to be precious in its entirety, but we're going to go back to that some other time. 65 ter number 09893, please. In Serbian it is page 11 -- rather, 14, and -- in English it is 14, actually, and in Serbian it's 11. D545. It was admitted that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us switch to e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now have a look at this. Your conclusion was that in this case the shell was fired from positions held by the Army of Republika Srpska and that the range was 2400 metres; right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On this particular page the conclusion is that at a range of 2400 metres puts the firing position in the hills, which is out of earshot of the UN observers due to the lay of the land. You say that they would not have heard the round being fired due to the hills and valleys; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that it was proven before this court that a stabiliser has to remain at the point of explosion when the third charge is involved? Do you agree with that finding?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'm not aware that that finding has been made, and if the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not either, but with that caveat, whether you can answer the question, irrespective of whether or not it has been proven.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whether or not the tail fins will be at the point of impact is dependent on many, many factors. Normally at the lower to medium charges, percentage-wise, a higher percentage of the explosion would cause the tail fins to be blown away from the initial impact area and possibly be laying around within the close proximity of that strike. When firing on higher charges, i.e., charges 5 and 6, and the increased velocity that the round will have, you then have a higher percentage that the tail fins will be embedded within the crater. So in this particular case there is no surprise that the tail fins were found in close proximity to the crater but not within it, again giving a possible indication that the mortar was fired on possibly a low or medium charge only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, could you assist in what is the weight? We know the diameter. What is the weight of a 120 or 122-millimetre mortar round high explosive.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are all different types of round, Your Honour. It depends on what type they are, but they could range, well, approximately 20 to 30 kilogrammes. So quite a heavy round.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: And of that how much of that would be high explosive if it was a high explosive round.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I haven't got those figures in front of me, but high explosive content contained within that only probably about 3 or 4 kilogrammes of that, the main mass being made up of the steel belting that surrounds the explosive content.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: And just for analysis, in terms of the explosive effect, would that be similar, less, or more than, say, 155-millimetre artillery shell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be less and a different type of explosion effect. With mortars being designed for main use, which is antipersonnel, their bodies are designed to fragment into smaller pieces than artillery ammunition which fragments are generally larger and with a larger blast effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, how many charges are needed, then, for this shell to get there from a distance of 2400 metres?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To arrive at that range charges 3, 4, 5, and 6 would be able to achieve that range.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where was this stabiliser found? How far away was it from the point of explosion?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no measurement of that. You saw from the video that it was laying in the road, obviously some distance from the point of impact, but I have not been shown any direct or detailed measurements on exactly how far away it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What would you expect it to be, given all these elements that you have established?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be any distance away. It depends on the angle at which, of course, it was blown away. And in this case, because fired within streets, it could have obviously bounced back off buildings to end up where it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the distance at which the stabiliser was could also have been an element for establishing the angle, right, in view of what you said a moment ago that it depends on the angle, it depends on how far it will get away or bounce away?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Where the tail fins are found, you could not just that to determine in any way whatsoever the angle, because it could, for many different reasons, really end up anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall that in the case of Markale I it was established that the stabiliser, when it arrives with such force with a charge of at least 3, has to remain stuck in the crater?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. With Markale I, the tail fins were still in the crater. And as I mentioned a few minutes ago, this has a higher percentage chance of happening when a mortar is fired on a higher charge and therefore arriving in the ground at a higher velocity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall that at Markale I the angle of descent was very similar? It was a 120-millimetre shell, and the charge was at least 3. There were at least three charges; right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: With Markale I, because we had no accurate angle to determine the descent, they worked the angle out from the minimum, which it must have been, to clear the buildings and then came up with all the possibilities. And with Markale I, they looked at all possibles from charge 1 through to charge 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what kind of injuries persons who had been standing there would sustain if they were standing one metre away from the point of impact of a 122-millimetre shell? Would limbs have been amputated?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just -- to clarify, we're talking here about a 120-millimetre mortar, not a 122-millimetre shell, because that is an artillery shell. That is completely different. But within a 120-millimetre mortar, if you would right next to it as well as damage caused by the shrapnel, the fragmentation, you would also have damage caused by the blast. So you'd have blast injuries as well as shrapnel injuries.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would it be possible to have body parts fully amputated, and if that is the case, how would you explain that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the directions of blast and the -- the higher content of shrapnel which will have closer into the round, that is how you would possibly have cause of main body parts being amputated and, of course, high degrees of damage. The further you would then get away from the point of burst the blast effects will then be minimised, and you'd then predominantly see more shrapnel injuries.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yesterday we saw that film. Is that the usual way casualties are being dealt with when such incidents occur? Do you remember how these people were piled up, dragged down the streets to trucks? Just give a yes or no answer. Is that the usual way things are done?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no set way of -- of clearing a scene where civilians are involved, as they will do whatever they think they need to do at the time, and they will obviously use whatever resources they have to clear the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I go back to the term I used from the very outset, taking care of casualties. I'm not talking about clearing the terrain.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 09917. Could we have that, please? Page 3 both in Serbian and in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It was established -- rather, you established, right, that -- that UNPROFOR headquarters sent a report about this incident at a request sent by the UN. 09917 is the number. And over here in paragraph 4 of this report it says -- can we see paragraph 4. Yes, we have it both in Serbian and in English. Yesterday you confirmed that you know what Cymbeline radar is. Can you please read this part of paragraph 4 where there's a reference to that radar.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 4 states that: "The evidence from Cymbeline radar was used by the UNPROFOR G2 staff to ascertain the firing range of the mortars. At that time of the firing, the incident -- the radar was operation on a direction arc and at an angle that would have detected the trajectory of any mortar fired at a range of 950 metres or less and showed that the round fired from 900 metres would have reached vertex height on its trajectory, which would have registered on the radar beam. The assessment was that the mortars were fired at a lower trajectory which passed under the radar beam. Any round fired at such a trajectory could pass under the radar beam would have come from a firing position, dependent on charge, at a range between 1500 and 3500 metres. The distance to the confrontation line from the impact point is 1050 metres."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that all -- all shells that are about 950 metres would have been registered by this radar?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not the case, because Cymbeline works on the angle of the vertex height. The vertex height on some of the other trajectories, as the Cymbeline report here mentions, although fired further away, their vertex height could have been lower than the round that fired only 950 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You're talking about indirect fire, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The term "indirect fire" suggests that whoever fired this round, that they could not see the target. You must remember that mortars can fire what is called direct fire. The term "indirect fire" has no -- does not relate to the arc or the path in which the round takes from firing to when it hits the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that UNPROFOR organs and investigation organs of Bosnia and Herzegovina established that the angle of descent of this shell due to the height of the building had to be 67 or more than 67 degrees? By no means could it have been less than 67 degrees; right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D2231. Could we have that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see this table referring to charges? We see 120-millimetre shell trajectories from charge 1 to charge 6 if -- if the descent angle is 67 degrees. The range is from 900 to 4700 metres. Does this table correspond to your knowledge of this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've not seen this table before, and I obviously don't know who's produced this, so I couldn't either confirm or deny this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm the firing tables that 900 metres is 0 plus 1 and 1700 is 0 plus 2 and so on and so forth? Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Without having the firing tables in front of me and the precise figures, it wouldn't be possible to confirm the exact ranges. These look approximately correct. Well, as I say, I cannot confirm the exact ranges you will get at that degrees by charge without having the range tables.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you stated for the record that charge 3 corresponds to 2400 metres; right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That is in your report as well; right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is the radar beam, this line that we see, and it has to do with charge 1, although according to the UNPROFOR report it can be even lower because there are also lower directions or arcs in this respect. However, in this case, the angle of descent would have to be less than 67 degrees, so that option is ruled out. Do you agree that the shell could not have been fired with a charge of 0 plus 1 from the Serb positions because the line of separation was at a distance of at least 1050 metres in that direction?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. A range of 900 metres would be within the confrontation lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Into Muslim territory; right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the assumption that the direction of the shell was established properly, and that's where the range was over 1.000 metres; right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The established of range came up with different variables because we obviously have the minimum descent angle of 67 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that if this trajectory were to be below the radar's beam, the peak of the arc, if it were lower, then it would have -- that would not have been the case because the building that was in the vicinity; right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've obviously got no data regarding the radar beam and how that works, where it was pointing or anything else. You would obviously have to get the Cymbeline experts to answer that particular point. But if a round was fired at lower than 67 degrees, then, yes, it would not have cleared the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid that my question was not quite clear, but you felt what it was that I was getting at. So you agree that every shell whose trajectory would go below the first line of 900 metres would have a shorter range and an angle of descent of less than 67 degrees; right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure on your question, but regardless of which charge was fired, it must have had an elevation on it greater than 67 degrees, obviously it would not have cleared that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you agree that according to UNPROFOR findings their observation radar was able to record a round flying along the first trajectory and also all the higher trajectories?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The information I have is as per the reports where the Cymbeline people reported that where their radar was pointing at the time, that in their opinion they would not have detected the round being fired at the distance of 900 metres -- sorry, they would have detected the round being fired at a range of 900 metres but they believe they would not have heard the round being fired at the medium charges or medium ranges that they suggest in their report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You're trying to say that even from a higher distance and with the same angle a round could fly even on a lower trajectory than these 548 metres.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say it could fly lower than that 548 metres you have on this drawing. The angles they fire at are specifically laid out in the range tables. The maximum vertex height those rounds may achieve along their path will be listed in those range tables.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you agree that if it were fired from 900 metres and landed at 67 degrees or more, then it would have to be as shown here, over 548 metres elevation. The vertex height would have been more?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The vertex height of the round fired on charge 1 to achieve that angle of descent, 67 degrees. I don't know whether it is the 548 as shown here but it will be, of course, specified in the range tables, and it will be listed in those range tables at that angle for that charge the maximum vertex height that that round would be able to achieve.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, if it is convenient, it's time to take a break.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is convenient, but we will have to finish with this subject because it's important. And if I may ask Mr. Higgs to get these tables during the break, because this was done according to the table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll have a break for half an hour. There's something the Chamber needs to discuss during the break. So we'll resume at 5 past 10.00 -- five past 11.00 I should say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was informed that, Mr. Karadzic, you have something to raise.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Excellency. To be able to take full advantage of the presence of my expert, could you approve that the entire team may be present during the breaks so I can use the breaks to consult with them and prepare?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you be clearer as to the meaning of "entire team"?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, so far only my privileged advisors, Mr. Robinson and Mr. Sladojevic, were able to be with me, and now I would like you to approve in a Ms. Subotic and experts who are part of the team may also join me during the breaks. There is problem with OLAD and they need your decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As it concerns the security issues, the Chamber does not want to make the decision lightly, and given that the testimony of this witness is almost coming to an end and that only today we have only one break left, so the Chamber is minded to make an informed decision having -- after having heard from the various organs of the Tribunal so will make its ruling tomorrow. Let's bring in the witness. Do you have any say, Mr. Gaynor, or Mr. Tieger, as to this issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We take no position on the matter, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning still. Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we get back 1D2231.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting, Mr. Higgs, what was decisive in determining this angle of descent, 67 degrees? Do you agree that it was the height of the roof of the building?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two pieces of evidence, the calculations of the height of the building and the ballistic calculation conducted by the forensic team, one of -- the first which came up with 67 degrees, the second of which came up with an angle of approximately 70 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that according to all these findings, particularly because of the height of the building the angle of descent could not be less than 67 degrees regardless of the distance?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May I ask you to draw in before the -- below the vertex height of this first trajectory, to draw the building so we can picture it more easily.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whereabouts do you want the building drawing?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Between this line, 900 and 67 degrees, to see that the height of the building was decisive in determining the minimum angle. Do you see the vertex height of this first trajectory, 900 metres?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, Mr. Higgs. Mr. Higgs confirmed or agreed that according to all these findings because of the height of the building the angle of descent could not be less than 67 degrees regardless of the distance. However, the witness was not able to confirm what this -- this diagram or picture depicts as it is now, so what's the point of asking the witness to mark the height of the building on this document? If Mr. Gaynor is not going to oppose to the admission of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, actually I was going to make some submissions about this document at the appropriate moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We can mark this document for identification for future identification by Defence witnesses. At this moment, speaking for myself, it is not mature to be admitted at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, well, in that case, if I could just make my brief submissions now. First of all, it appears to have been prepared by somebody within the Defence team in this case to support the Defence case. I just want that clear on the record. Second, there's currently no evidence to support the parabolas described and represented on this document, the six parabolas described. There's no evidence on the record to support the centre point of the radar beam, there's no evidence to support the radius of the radar beam, and the figure of 548 metres mentioned is not based on evidence on the record so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So I would like you to proceed after marking this identification for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D548 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, this is very important point. There are three -- or, rather, four very hard facts that the angle was determined by the height of the building. If the distance is greater, 2400 or 2700, if the round came, obviating this radar beam, then the angle would have been greater than 67 or 70 degrees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I see your point, but the problem is that the witness is not able to confirm the location or the position of the radar beam as reflected in this diagram. Am I correct, Mr. Higgs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just have to correct the record. It would have been lower than 67 degrees. If the range had been greater in order to avoid the radar beam, the round would have come in at less than 67 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Maybe you did not receive the interpretation. Do you agree with my proposition?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, this diagram represents if -- to get the angle of 67 degrees, you can achieve it on all charges. So if you wanted to achieve an angle greater than that to clear the building, the large -- all the larger charges, charges say from 1 to 6 can all do that depending, of course, on how far away the mortar was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But the angle was determined by the height of the building. Could this round have come to land at this place with the lower trajectory under the same angle in view of the building, or it would have gone through the building in that case?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At an angle less than 67 degrees, the round would not have cleared the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the radar, as we were able to see from the UN report, was working. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document has received a number, hasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. It was marked for identification as Exhibit D548.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In view of the fact that we are probably not going to have enough time, we have to move to the second incident now, and that's the incident in the queue for water in Sana Babovic Street, 12 July 1993. Can we get 1D2242.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, is this the site of this incident, including these elements?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen this photograph before. It's not a photograph I was given as part of my investigation, so it would be very difficult for me to either confirm or deny it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And on what basis did you study this incident?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the reports that I mention in my consolidated report, the investigations carried out by the two teams that were present at the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Local investigators established that the projectile came from north-west, from the direction of Nedzarici. The UNPROFOR determined that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic repeat his question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, could you repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Local investigators established that the round came from north-west, from the direction of Nedzarici. The UNPROFOR determined that the round came from a direction whose bearing would be 500 100 thousandths parts and that makes 287 degrees, and that's this line marked here. Did you accept that this was indeed the direction from which the round came?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On looking at the two reports, because of the poor quality of information due to the round exploding within a person, and they then calculating their bearings from the patterns given by the shrapnel on the surrounding areas, I have no reason to doubt their findings that the round came from westerly, I believe north-westerly location.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now get 65 ter 11394. The photograph we need is ERN 1026897. The photograph should be 1026897. Yes, that's the photograph. We need just one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you, Mr. Higgs, mark on this photograph the likely direction from which the projectile came.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not possible from the photograph, because it doesn't show obviously the marks in any great detail or the surrounding area to give any possible direction just from that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now get back 1D2242. The previous document. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could this assist you if you looked at a picture with markings of the places of the incident and the bearing established by the UNPROFOR? Do you see that the angle is an acute angle relative to the payment?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you can tell from the -- the two reports that are in evidence that I refer to, the two investigation teams do come up with slightly different bearings due to the type of crater that we had not being very accurate to determine bearing, and that's why they have only given general bearings in this particular case, and that is why you get a slight difference between the two reports. But from the pictures that we have alone, it's not possible for me to either confirm or deny the investigations carried out on the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I dispute it. I dispute these investigations. I cannot take it on trust. The Defence now has to establish whether was indeed so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get back 11394, the photograph. 65 ter 113694. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark on this photograph the fragments of the round on the asphalt? The typing here says: "Close-up of the place of incident, the centre of explosion, after the removal of the casualties."

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see some of the fragments in the tarmac here, but obviously due to the quality of the picture and its angle, you cannot see any of the other markings that may be on the car or the fence. Do you wish me just to mark the markings in the tarmac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. All the traces you can identify. This is a photograph that they provided to you and when you worked on the basis of this photo, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I did not use the photographs as part of my determination because of, again, their poor quality and not sharing really any evidence I could base any findings upon. But pieces of shrapnel in the payment are ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Just mark the traces.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. Difficult to identify pieces of shrapnel marks and pieces of debris that are laying on the road. But the three I have identified seem to be just three parts made by pieces of shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I draw your attention to the left side of the photograph. Do you see the trolley, the cart that people used to transport water? Can you mark the direction of the force that overturned this trolley?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The trolley you are relating to, I believe, are these wheels here, and it seems to be tipped over in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, on the right corner of this car, which is a Skoda, can you mark the direction of the force which deformed the rear right headlight or light? Do you see that this is the rear of the automobile? It's deformed by the explosion. Can you tell us the direction of the force which deformed the chassis and the rear right light?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears that the round has exploded obviously very close to the car, and the damage would indicate probably slightly to the rear of the car so that some of the blast has gone into the rear of the car. Impossible from this picture to give a definite angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But can you mark whether it was from the top or from the bottom looking just at this damage?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just looking at the damage, no. Difficult to tell whether the blast was above, below, or in line. The photograph does not give enough information to determine that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it look like this blast was below or above? Does this look caved in or raised?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you purely look at the boot of the car, it does give the impression that some force was pushing down in one corner, which may indicate that the blast could have been slightly higher than the level of the boot of the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you also see the left-hand side of the boot? Can you mark on it the direction of the force which caused this damage?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said before, it's very difficult to be precise with the direction of force as there's not enough information purely in this photograph, but it could possibly indicate that the force has been, as I said, slightly downwards and probably off to one side, in this direction here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you write the date and your initials at the bottom of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Marks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. As Exhibit D549.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now get 65 ter 11394, which is the same document only a page further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will keep this image first.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next page, please. [In English] Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. They are having difficulties in keeping the previous image first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: They lost the image, but they are confident to be able to revive it through the assistance of the image taken by the video. Then we'll -- we can proceed. Let's go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, can you mark on this photograph the rib trace on the joint of the two edges. The edge of the pavement. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean some of the shrapnel marks that are on the -- on the tarmac?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No. Do you see this part which looks like stairs. The step at the top of that there are fragment scrapes, like ribs.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean these marks here? It keeps moving down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To assist you, may I ask the usher to give you this photograph. You will be then able to identify what I mean.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ones you have circled, that area there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Is that a fragment scrape?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the quality of the photograph, I could not say that it is or whether it's from some form of previous damage. The photograph does not make that clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we are not going to tender that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get 65 ter 11394, page with the number ending 893. It's page 2 the document. It's marked with an ERN number ending in 893. The full ERN number is 10268893. No. This is 94. We need 93. We'll need this photo too later, but now we need the one ending in 893. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you notice this white car with doors open?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the car in the centre of the photograph, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now get a zoom-in on the doors. This open door, was it damaged by fragments of a bomb in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Purely from the photograph, often you can see holes or marks in the door. Whether or not, of course, that is from this incident I cannot obviously confirm or deny. Whether or not it was caused by this particular mortar bomb, again with this clarity and without having fragments to identify, it's impossible to say whether it is or it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that this car in the photograph is moved towards the fence and it's basically leaning against the fence? The rear of the car, that is. The front is on the driveway. The front part is on the driveway, whereas the middle of the body of the car is on the sidewalk, right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess the car does appear to be in a position half on and half off the pavement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have the next page, please. Could I please have the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see the Skoda here? And in front of it you can see the car with the door open; right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To the right-hand side the photograph, you can just see the edge of the open door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please mark that trolley now, the one that was tipped over, and these two cars.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The trolley wheels that we marked before are there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you show us where the body of the trolley is? Can you show it to us now, and can you show the direction in which the trolley fell.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The trolley location appears to be in that location, and appears to have fallen over that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark the door on the previous car? It can be seen here as well. Not as clearly as in the previous photograph, but you can still see the open door.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The edge of the door appears to be in that location there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that the white car behind the Skoda, the one that you marked just now, or actually that between these two cars is the gate that was used to access the water pump, and can you show the direction of that gate?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the previous photograph, the first one that we looked at, the gate is in the fence somewhere just off the edge of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, but that's the arrow. That's the projection. Do you agree that if an 82-millimetre shell hits a man who is standing and explodes that, do you agree that that body is going to behave in a certain way according to relevant laws? Is it going to move in a certain way, or is it just going to remain standing there as it was?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What happens to the body when hit by obviously a mortar round will depend on, again, many circumstances; how the person may have been standing at the time, where the round may have impacted on the body, the angle descent of the round. All these factors will affect where any remains may end up on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And in which direction, then, will the body fall in relation to the trajectory along which the round moved in the first place.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again for the same reasons as my previous answer, depending where it hit on the body the blast effect would probably have the biggest motion effect on the body. So depending where the round hit this lady, as I believe it was, would affect where her remains would end up on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: According to everything you know, which one of these bodies had been hit?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the -- the reports I read, it gave no final positions of the pieces. However, from reading the reports, I would assume that it is the body that is to the rear and right next to the car. To the rear right of the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark the body and could you mark the axis in relation to the position of that body.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The body, I believe, and again this is only obviously from written reports, I've never had this confirmed, but I believe it would be -- that's one that may have received the strike of the mortar round, but it's obviously been covered in plastic. So how that now lays on the ground, I cannot see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is the site before the bodies were moved? They're just covered in plastic; right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears to be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
