utterances.text: Could we please ask you to put the date here and to initial this. Could you actually place a mark on this photograph next to the head of this person that had been hit, in your opinion.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And also in terms of the orientation of this body.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give any definite of which way round the bodies laying because of it's being covered in plastic. It could be laying in any direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But can you mark the axis in terms of how this body lies?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're referring to the points which I marked with the X, it -- obviously he's just a -- a shape covered in plastic. I would be guessing if I was to give it any form of direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He says he doesn't know. Let's proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, he doesn't know where the head is but the axis of the body could be established, but all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is the position of this body below letter x and also below the trolley?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, the two other pieces covered in plastic, because they're covered up their orientation could be one way or the other. Their heads or feet could be at either end. That is really all I could ascertain from the picture.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D550, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. If there's enough time, we are going to offer some footage from Croatian television of this site before the plastic covers were placed. We're not even going to ask how come the TV crew was there so fast, but it all really depends on the time we have left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Don't make a speech, Mr. Karadzic. We'll have 15 minutes before we take the next break.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Then I will have to move on to another incident. It is incident number 4 in attachment G. It's the football game in Dobrinja on the 1st of June, 1993. Could we please have in e-court --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Actually, Mr. Higgs, before we find the document that we're looking for, in the beginning -- or, rather, in the -- in the first part of your report did you say that you used documents that you marked as references A, B, and C?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't got my document in front of me, so I'm not clear what references are you discussing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you actually visit that particular location where the incident occurred at the football game in Dobrinja on the 1st of June, 1993? Did you visit that particular location when you went out there now?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who did you visit it with?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was taken there by the UN team at the time, the names of which are in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say: "At the request of the International Tribunal, I visited the location with Mr. Chester Stamp, and I explored the two craters concerned." Can you tell us who Mr. Stamp is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He works obviously here as part of ICTY. I am not sure what his specific role is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was it that you found on this site? What kind of traces did you find that you used in your work afterwards?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was taken to the site to have a look at the general area and what buildings are around. The craters of the mortars, obviously due to many years passing between the incident and me attending, had by this time been filled with a rubber-type material. So therefore, any detailed crater analysis by myself obviously was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This rubber-type material, was it placed there intentionally in order to preserve the craters as it was?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason why it's been put in there obviously I don't know. It was put in not to preserve them as far as any analysis work is concerned. It may have been put in to just preserve them so people know where they landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you carry out any measurements in terms of the crater, the angle of descent and so on?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Determination the crater, no, because obviously they were filled with this material, and therefore crater examination would not be possible, but I did work out the minimum angle of descent to the buildings because the nearby flats was one of the calculations used by the examination team to calculate a minimum angle around must have achieved to clear those buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So without doing any measuring on your own you accepted their findings; right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The only measurement I took was the minimum angle or the crater examination information. I accepted -- I had no reason not to accept the -- the investigation team's information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you just trusted them fully. Isn't that right? On the face of it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to believe that what they're writing is true and it's been calculated honestly. I can do as much as I can from visiting the scene and looking at their reports, and there was nothing in their reports that stood out as being grossly inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in such matters repeated measuring has to yield similar results like in any science? Every scientific fact has to be proven time and again by repeating measuring.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That would obviously give you more accuracy should you be able to measure something more than once. In this case here, obviously only the teams attending the site had that opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you did not measure anything, let me ask you whether you took any photographs when you were there.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the positions are of these two craters, and could you sketch their respective positions vis-à-vis each other on the screen?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be a guess at the moment from my, obviously, recollection of this incident and when I was there many years ago. So it would not be a very accurate sketch, but, yes, I can proceed with the best of my recollection, if required.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please do that, and could the registry help you with that. Could you do that on a blank screen, and could you try to say what the approximate distance is as well as the position of the craters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we not have pictures of the site?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: There is a fairly comprehensive report relating to this incident which was admitted through an earlier witness. I don't have the number with me. And secondly, we see no point whatsoever in asking the witness to conduct this exercise. It seems to be totally pointless.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: I agree too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you will have had three hours by quarter past 12.00, which was assigned to you for your cross-examination of Mr. Higgs. I take it that you're going to conclude by quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can stop by 12.15, but I cannot conclude by 12.15. This is very important. This expert did not check or did not conduct any measurements in terms of findings of other investigation teams. The Defence has this unavoidable need to throw more light on eight incidents that are included in this indictment and in other indictments, and they have also become part of different judgements. So when are we going to do it if not now, and that would fall within the 20 hours that the Defence asked for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, as is apparent from the line of questions we saw right now, or as we made it clear yesterday in our ruling, the evidence of this witness is of limited nature. There's no point, as you put it, robust questions to this witness because this witness has limited knowledge. So after the break we'll give you another half an hour. So arrange your questions to be concluded in that time limit. Judge Morrison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, obviously Mr. Higgs is of great expertise as far as mortars are concerned and everything related to mortars. It's an impressive curriculum vitae, if I may say so, but inevitably in this case he was relying very heavily upon investigations which had already been done. He didn't have the opportunity to do original investigations because patently he wasn't there to do it. So the cross-examination seems to me to be necessary to be focused on the methodology he used to verify the original findings rather than asking him to go back now and try and, as it were, do an original report which is not fair on him and it's really of no assistance to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, the basic methodology of this witness is trust in the findings of previous teams, and that was stated quite clearly. So there is no methodology involved. There is trust. There is belief. He is taking over without any further checks the findings of previous teams, and he is simply taking this at face value, carte blanche. These are mortar incidents. In this case and in this entire situation in Sarajevo, the most important ones are the mortar incidents. They're the ones that harmed us the most, and they have to be explored one by one because we claim, the Defence claims, that none of these incidents were caused by the Serb side. They were designed for the purpose of bringing the Serb side into a difficult position -- into a difficult position and to invoke sympathy on the part of the international community and to bring about intervention, and we're going to prove it that way. This kind of improvisation and sloppiness exhibited by the teams in Sarajevo was aimed at propaganda, and they were speaking to the public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: You're simply making speeches and wasting what little time you have left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will have a break now for half an hour. After which you'll have half an hour to conclude your cross-examination of Mr. Higgs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we continue, Judge Morrison has a question for Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor, is it the Prosecution's intent to call evidence from the original investigating teams as to the findings they made and the methodology that they used?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, it is our intent to call several of the investigators. I don't want to say that we're going to call every author of every report that we've tendered, but we will be calling a number of investigators.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that, because of course what this witness can do with his expertise is to confirm the methodology that was used, examine the reports to see if there are any obvious errors in the way that the report was calculated or structured and give his, as it were, imprimatur as to that aspect of it. What he doesn't do by virtue of his testimony is to prove the original findings themselves. He simply, as it were, says that as far as he can see, the methodology that was used and the conclusions drawn from those -- that methodology, which of course he has to accept as he has said, because he has no reason not to accept it, that doesn't prove it so that I'm glad to hear you, in fact, going to be calling additional evidence as to that point, and I thought I'd raise that now to put Dr. Karadzic's mind at rest, because with great respect I think he has been labouring under the slight misapprehension that this witness's evidence conclusively proves the matters set out in the original reports which it doesn't. It simply adds a gloss to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. There will be a significant number of other witnesses that Dr. Karadzic will be able to cross-examine concerning the findings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gaynor. Thank you, Judge Morrison. Mr. Karadzic, as I said to you, you will have half an hour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now I feel a bit better having heard this clarification. However, the Defence would expect to be in a position to cross-examine investigators who worked on every one of the incidents that are in the indictment. For the sake of credibility and the general situation, we would even like to deal with investigators who worked on incidents that the OTP took out of my indictment, and we ask for that with good reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, you did visit the location in Dobrinja. What kind of a surface was the one that you saw there where these rounds landed?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The improvised football pitch area was made of tarmac, tarmacadam.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The second one?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both the rounds fell in the area of the football pitch, so they both fell on the tarmac surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 10105. That's the 65 ter number. We have both a Serbian version, 10105. That's the 65 ter number. And the page is 03 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Dr. Karadzic please repeat the number. It is too fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat the page number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 03058877. The findings of Captain Houdet. I don't know how you pronounce the name. This is not the document. It would help us if 03058877 -- that would be the right page, whereas this one ends in 356. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about trying page 18 of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's try it. It may be helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to what Captain Houdet is saying. 81 millimetres. Let us look at this. Due to macadam, there can be no fuse furrow. So how do we reconcile the two, asphalt and macadam?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, what is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who's right, you or Captain Houdet? You say tarmac asphalt and he says macadam, and he says that the angle of descent and range cannot be determined because there is no fuse furrow.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct because of the -- the hardness of the surface. He could not work out a precise angle of descent, which is why then he went on to work out what the minimum angle could have been, in this case against the top of the buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So it's not asphalt or tarmac. It's macadam, right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think what he calls macadam, he's -- what I would call tarmac, I think it's just a translation issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, I think it's confusion. Macadam was the name of the Scottish engineer who invented substance that's also known as tarmac. Simply tarmac is a word for macadam.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then this is a linguistic confusion, because the same word "macadam," as we pronounce it, means something completely different. It's a different kind of surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that one of the Muslim documents says that this red mass was placed in the craters in order to preserve them for investigation? We can find the document, but it's part of the documents contained in your report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Objection. First of all, I don't believe that the red substance which one sees in Sarajevo today was placed in these crater sites to preserve them for investigation. It's more a memorial purpose. And second, Mr. Karadzic wishes to refer to the documents that he's talking about. I really must ask for a page number in this instance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall the incident at Alipasino Polje. 22nd of January, 1994. Do you remember that incident?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you just confirm which incident this one was as just by date and a location doesn't register with me immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: G, incident number 6.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Was this the incident with the -- the children in the street?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How many shells were fired on that day, Mr. Higgs?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the investigations, they ascertain that there were a total of three rounds fired.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D021522, please, in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honour, the report by Captain Houdet, which the witness has just commented upon, has been admitted as page 9 of P1053 through an earlier witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this map, Mr. Higgs?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not. I've not seen this map before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the basis of which map did you check the findings that you confirmed, the findings of the investigation organs of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the exact map which I -- which I used at the time. Obviously I was working from the data supplied to me by the investigations of the locations. I visited the area, checked it against the information that they had come to in their investigations, but as I say, this particular map isn't unfamiliar to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Is not unfamiliar or it is familiar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think unfamiliar. Yeah, unfamiliar Your Honour. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: It is not unfamiliar or familiar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Unfamiliar. I've not seen this particular map before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you refer us to the map on the basis of which you accepted the bearing?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not use a map for confirming bearings. That was done by looking at the initial reports and what they came to, looking at what remains of the shelter craters and where they are, and from that agreeing with the directions that were produced by the investigating team.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did they determine the bearing in their reports?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did. The reports here you have again approximate directions if I remember right from this particular incident, because the location of where the craters struck the ground did not produce quality craters for determining accurate bearings, so they used them to come up with an estimated direction from which the rounds could have come.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you to mark several points here. Do you see these three-wing buildings that represent the students' hostel?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just by looking obviously at the area or map with obviously the passage of time, I could not now without plotting the information and, again without guessing, of which of these building are the ones that we are referring to in this particular incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Do you agree that where it says Alipasino Polje, do you know how many storeys these buildings have?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The exact number of storeys, no. I know they are obviously blocks of flats, but no, not the total number of storeys.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But it's more than six, seven, or eight; right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, from memory I cannot remember how many storeys these buildings have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you see those buildings? Have you been to this place?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to the road where the rounds landed and walked around the general area, but again which of those buildings precisely I went to I couldn't tell you just from looking at this -- this aerial view of the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you go to the place from which this projectile was allegedly fired, and it's called the Institute for Blind Children?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't visit the area of the institute for the blind, only the area of where the incident occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina ballistic experts established that the projectile came from the west, from Nedzarici, that is to say, the area of the Institute for Blind Children. Since you have not been there, we can no longer establish whether it's true or not, but did you accept that the azimuth, the bearing, was 180?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two points here. First of all, by visiting the area, Nedzarici, where they suspected it may have been fired from, would not have helped me in my determining if it could have been fired from there or not. So therefore I based my opinion, of course, on the forensic reports based around strikes on the ground, and again because of the poor quality. That is why they only gave an approximate area of where they suspected it came from rather than a detailed bearing back from the crater back to a possible firing point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just a small correction to the transcript. It was 270 degrees, not what is written. But can we agree about one thing? Do see on the map where it's written "Institute for Blind Children"? It's west of Alipasino Polje. Do you see where it "Oslobodjenje," and do you see where it says "Studentski Dom," students' hostel?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see where it says "Alipasino Polje"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A little to the west do you see three-winged buildings where it says "Studentski Dom"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would it be easy if I mark this on the map of where I'm looking?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. It says "Zavod" here, a bit to the north it says "Oslobodjenje," and then there are two three-winged buildings where it says "Studentski Dom." May I offer it -- offer you this map where it's marked so you can see it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is the three wing-building you are referring to the red one, the small red one in the centre, that one there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No. No. East of that, the large building is the building of "Oslobodjenje," and it's written there. Right. Here, may I try to assist you. This drawing is marked. Can we erase this marking. Do you see where "Oslobodjenje" is now; the students hostel, Studentski Dom; and Zavod, the Institute for Blind Children?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the three markings that you have put on this map, which is the three-wing building and the large building in the centre. The small one just underneath.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know under whose control this large building and the three-wing buildings were?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the time, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the confrontation line was?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not without, again, studying the maps of the confrontation lines. I can't remember at this stage where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that relative to this smallest building down here, the Institute for Blind Children, the buildings of "Oslobodjenje" and the students' hostel were a little to the north?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If the -- if the building further south on there is the institute for the blind, then obviously the other two buildings are a little distance to the north of them, or to the north of that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see where it says "Nedzarici" below?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the main name of "Nedzarici," yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you just mark "Alipasino Polje"? Was it with the first group of buildings or the second group of buildings that the bomb landed? Is it nearer to the western or the eastern group of buildings?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my recollection, again without studying the maps, it'd be unsure, but it was the buildings on the eastern side of that square.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you mark that. You are right. It's in the eastern ring. That's where Cetinjska Street is.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously the exact grid and location is shown in the reports, but by recollection it would be in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That would be south-west. Cetinjska Street is near the petrol station where it's marked. Alipasino Polje has two blocks shaped as 8s. You see the rings of the 8s. Do you see where Cetinjska Street is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, given the lack of detailed knowledge about geography of the witness about this place, I don't think this line of questions lead us anywhere. Put your direct question, if necessary, and move on your next item.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you go to Cetinjska Street where the bombs landed and did you see the craters?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I went to the street. Obviously the craters have deteriorated over the number years, and so therefore couldn't really use those in any whatsoever to help me, but I did go have a look at the general area, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you normally keep a mortar on the forward front line in urban conditions?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where they would be locate would depend on various factors. You would want to try and keep your mortars as close as possible to the front line so the range of the mortar could then be used to cover a larger area, but you would not want to place it in harm's way. So you would not want to put it in a position where it would be obviously targeted by the opposing side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your report you wrote the following: "If these two mortars were active within one combat assignment, then it looks like it was a deliberate attempt to kill civilians in that area by forcing them, first of all, to run for cover and then by targeting their path. If that is in issue, then that was a deliberate ambush." Does this claim of yours imply full visibility of the place which you are targeting?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the three rounds were fired as one mission, and of course we do not know that, but if they were, we're in the position then of the 82-millimetre rounds landed in the street right outside the -- or close to the entrance to the buildings, may represent the three, as you said there, could be used together as a form of an ambush, but to do this, yes, you're right, that whoever fired it would ideally want to be able to see the area of where the rounds landed so they fire this at the right time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll deal with the rest when we get witnesses who made these reports. If they misled you, then it's their responsibility. Now, who suggested that you go to Mrkovici?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Was this for the Markale I incident?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise. Before that, can you put the date and your initials on this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think it will be of any assistance to us. He didn't mark it for himself. Let's do without this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Right. You are right. It's about Markale I. You said you had been to Mrkovici and that it was a possible site for an 82-millimetre mortar, but you couldn't find the place where it was dug in. Now, who suggested that you go to Mrkovici?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was to do with Markale I. I was looking for where this 120-millimetre mortar may have been fired from, because we had the whole range issue to try and ascertain. I looked around the areas within the Sarajevo town area, and then the United Nations people who were with me took me to the area, Nedzarici, because this is the area where if the mortars was fired on the higher charges, along that bearing line of 18 degrees is where it may have been sited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you have only three minutes. How long would you need for your redirect examination, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Approximately 20 minutes, no more than that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we get 1D2246.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We are again in Alipasino Polje. 1D2246, I want you to have a look at this. Do you accept, Mr. Higgs, that this is the Institute for Blind Children?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said earlier, I did not go to the institute of blind people, so I couldn't say whether it is or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that we see a rather high ground floor here and two upper floors?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a three-storey building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No point, Mr. Karadzic. He doesn't recognise this place.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. All right. But he'll recognise the next one. Can we now see 1D2245.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this picture familiar? Do we agree that this is the block of buildings in Alipasino Polje?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This could be the block of buildings. I have not seen it from this vantage point because I was on the road. So again, really from this photograph I couldn't really not either confirm or deny that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that apart from the ground floor there are seven or eight floors?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does appear. Obviously this has seven or eight floors, as best as you can tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you had been supplied with these two photographs and the photo of this photograph in the vicinity of the Institute for Blind Children, would you assume that there was full visibility from this place?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wherever the mortars were sited, which of course is what you get from the crater analysis, that is the position of the mortar, if somebody was directing this, an observer, they could have been anywhere. They don't have to be where the mortar is. An observer could have been in any area within visible line of sight of this particular area and not specifically where the mortar was actually fired from. So trying to identify where the observer was is nearly impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. But you know that this was under Muslim control, and the Institute for Blind Children was under Serbian control.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I'm aware, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you come across any information that in the investigations of these major incidents Serbian experts were involved?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've not seen any evidence to that fact, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that you were presented with the findings of the Bosnia-Herzegovina government, the Muslim government whose interest lay in laying the blame on the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The documents I was given obviously were the forensic -- the Bosnian forensic teams', and also the military teams that may be applicable on each site. Any reasons or intents on how they may have been produced, obviously I have no knowledge of at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But can you tell us what was the mandate given you by this Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was to look at the investigations that were conducted and see if their methodologies were correct, to see if there were any irregularities, as indeed there was on the Markale II case. And then by using my experience to give my opinion of were these cases correct, incorrect, and then again using my experience to see if I agree with findings or oppose, if need be, a different solution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you propose a different solution, different to the findings of the Muslim government investigation teams?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the case of Markale II, it wasn't a case of disagreeing with the Muslim authorities. It was disagreeing with the UNPROFOR reports, as that was the one that I believe is incorrect, so my findings agree with the first three investigations; that of the Muslim authorities, the UNPROFOR initial reports, and those of the French investigation team.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And during your site visit did you talk to anyone on the Serbian side about these incidents and these findings?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wasn't given an opportunity to speak to anyone from the Serbian side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you just explain one more thing, Mr. Higgs. How are you able to estimate the accuracy of the findings of the Muslim investigating teams without checking and conducting any measurements on site? How can you know that they did it accurately if you did not repeat their measurements? Is there any other method whereby you can establish that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the period of time where I was looking at the reports, I was working off the information that they have in their reports, and where possible seeing what they did, the results they got, and relating that to obviously the photographs of the areas, and on my visits obviously I did not carry out any measured analysis because the craters, of course, were not good enough condition when I was there. So my opinions are based upon their findings, their reports, and checks on the methodologies that they carried out which was why, again in the case of Markale II, why -- what the second reading stood out as being incorrectly obtained because the methodologies again for that one were -- were totally inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Was that your last question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I have one more question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the Markale case, or in the other cases, you did not make any measurements, but you still contested the findings of the United Nations and confirm the findings of the Muslim government. Why didn't you check in each and every case rather than confirm? Why were you able to -- to conduct your own analysis and checks in Markale and not in other cases?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Markale II specifically, the individual who carried out the second investigation, I had sight of his witness statement on how he conducted his investigation. On reading that statement, it was obvious that this person was not a mortar investigation expert, and he explains what he did, and he was using it totally incorrect and flawed procedures. That then led me to believe that the findings could be wrong. I then looked at other pieces of evidence like the photograph that we've already seen here to try and prove that as much as possible and see which of the findings then I most agree with. For the reasons I've already stated, I agree with the three investigation reports taken on the first day where they came to that bearing of 170 degrees and do not believe the bearing of the 220 to 240 because it is based on flawed methodologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karadzic. Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you ask some questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Judge Baird has some questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, I want to get back to Mrkovici just for a while. Now, yesterday's proceedings Dr. Karadzic asked you whether you were toured all the sites on the bearing between Mrkovici and Markale, whether you had toured other places to see if there were any suitable sites for a mortar, and you replied, and I quote: "We looked at all the area along that bearing line and identified the suitable places, yes." You recollect this, do you not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Now, how many places did you identify, Mr. Higgs?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We looked at all the areas that possibly could have been used to achieve that angle of descent, so there will be six areas in total from charge 1 out to the possibility of the area fired to charge 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Yes. And what -- what indicia or what parameters did you look for, if any, in order to arrive at the conclusion that any one place qualified as a possible location for the firing of that round?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- at the short ranges it would have obviously meant that the mortar would have been within the confrontation lines and within the built-up areas of Sarajevo, and we had no other reportings of noise or anything like that. At the middle two ranges, the medium charges, it would have placed the mortar in the area right on top of the confrontation line and for tactical reasons that is not an area where you would normally expect to see a mortar. The higher charges places it beyond the confrontation line in the area Mrkovici that we went to it have a look at. The other pieces of evidence that I had to take into account was the witness report who heard the mortar fire, and from that report he places it more at the higher charges than being within the area of Sarajevo, i.e., the lower charges, and they also took into account that the tail fins, the stabilisers of the mortar round, were imbedded into the crater. This happens on a high percentage of times when a mortar is fired on the higher charges. So using the sound -- the noise sound and that the fins were in the crater and that normally you would not expect people to shoot at their own civilians, all led me to believe in my opinion that the mortar was possibly fired from that area of Mrkovici on higher charges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: First of all, just to clarify a translation issue which came in earlier today concerning P1442, which -- no need to look at it now, but we were discussing the angle mentioned in the UN report which is 5100 mils. As Dr. Karadzic pointed out, that's approximately 287 degrees; you accept that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It sounds about right without doing the mathematical calculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Right. And just for the record, could you just confirm the number of mils in that complete revolution in the system you're using?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 6400 mils in a circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, I'm just going to ask you a couple of questions about Markale I, then Markale II, and yesterday you were shown a still photograph or a freeze from the video which was Exhibit D542, which was said to show covered stalls in Markale Market at some point prior to the beginning of the conflict. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that picture, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: All right. You were asked, and this is at pages 5953 and 5954, whether you stood by your finding based on previous investigations that it's possible with one hit of this market to land a shell without having the shell activate on the roofing plates. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd just like to show you three short clips from the video. I would like the first to be played now, please. This is from 65 ter 40125. And the first clip is E, 65 ter number 40125 E.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, as you can see from the bottom left that bears the date 5.2.1994. Do you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Play the next clip which is 65 ter number 40125 F?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What do you see there, Mr. Higgs?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a video just passed over the crater and it shows the pattern on the ground given by the shrapnel, and it shows them placing the stakes on the ground to indicate the direction of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That was at 6 minutes 50. We can play the rest of this clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And could I ask that the third clip now be played, which is 65 ter number 40125 G.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I just ask you to confirm the date on that third video is 6.2.1994?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, on the basis of those three clips that you've just watched, can you comment on the question of whether the projectile detonated upon impact with the ground or upon impact with some kind of roofing material?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From those pictures there, you can see that the -- the round has detonated on impact with the ground, and it seems to have landed like in a corridor between the stalls, so could quite easily have missed these roofing structures or whatever they may be.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to request the admission of those three clips into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. It's -- they themselves are excerpts of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The videos.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one moment. The Defence would like to know the provenance of these clips. When we produced similar clips we were asked to state the origin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I don't have that information to hand at this very moment. I can find it and provide it to the Court or directly to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get the entire footage from this -- from which this was excerpted, all the video material regarding all the incidents, especially Markale I and II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: From this conversation I take it that this was not previously disclosed to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: This is -- these are excerpts of 65 ter number 40125, which has been disclosed to the Defence, as well as a great number of other videos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The entire video of -- in the number of 65 ter number 40125 has been disclosed to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: A long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Let's proceed, and we can hear about the provenance of this video later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. Should we mark the excerpts for identification at this stage?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. I don't see any problem in admitting them right now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So, Your Honours, 65 ter 40125 E would be P1451. 65 ter number 40125 F would be P1452. And 65 ter 40125 G will be P1453.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: For the Court's benefit, this was delivered to the Prosecution in June 2001 from the AID service of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd now like to move to the Markale II incident, and I'd like video 65 ter 40221 to be brought up. And if we can go, first of all, to 1 minute and 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Higgs, as you can see there is the body of a person which was shown to you yesterday, and it was put to you that there was relatively little fluid under the body. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, earlier today you told the Court that there were two ways in which the impact of a projectile can cause death. One is through shrapnel, and the other is through blast; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, insofar as you're able to tell on the basis your expertise, is it true that death through blast injury can occur with minimal evidence of external injury?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from my experience, yes. Blast injuries can show very little external damage. Obviously, I don't have any evidence in this particular case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could we move now to location 6 minutes and 40 seconds, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What do you see in front of you there, Mr. Higgs?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It looks like the tail is section of a 120-millimetre round that is laying in the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, in cross-examining -- cross-examination yesterday you were asked a considerable number of questions about this item concerning, that is, the integrity of the item, and you said you couldn't tell from looking at this -- enough information to confirm some of the questions. So I'd like to now show you an object. If the usher could assist me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We hope that the Defence, too, will have a chance to see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. The Defence has inspected this specific object previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Proceed, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, could you describe what you're holding in your hand?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This looks like the tail section as you see on the still video. The tail section of a 120-millimetre mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you read out insofar as you can the markings on the bottom of the item?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have the mark or type, we have "Mike, Mike, Mike 74," and a batch number. It's difficult to read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What Mr. Higgs is seeing --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could be 9307.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What Mr. Higgs is seeing now what we see on our monitor, the very thing?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, yes. If Mr. Higgs is able to confirm that, yes, that is it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure how Mr. Higgs is able to confirm that, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well. I'm going to ask him some more questions which might enable him to confirm it. If could ask for P1449 to be brought up. I'd like to go to page 16 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Gaynor, how long would you, more, need to conclude?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Literally about two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The document which is coming up now in a moment is a report prepared by the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina Ministry of the Interior, Security Services Centre Sarajevo, and in that document as you'll see in a moment they describe the projectile recovered from the Markale II site. I'm waiting for page 16 in the English. Now, as you'll see, Mr. Higgs, if you look at approximately in the middle of the page you're looking at, it says: "One pair of fins is missing and three traces caused by shock-resistant welding are visible on that spot; 31.5 millimetre brass plate with one hole, around 6.2 millimetres in diameter. In the middle of the plate was found at the bottom two holes" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you read more slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: My apologies. "... two holes around 3.1 millimetres in diameter were on the side 10 millimetres away. A small brass cap around 2.5 millimetres in diameter with the trace of a crater-shaped impact is placed within a 6.2 millimetre inner hole. Two signs in Cyrillic are printed on the rim of the brass plate, MK, M74, and KB9307." Does that description agree with the object in your hand.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I have no further questions. I'd like to tender that object into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it as evidence in this -- in this case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P1454, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As well as the document we just saw?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I see this object?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Of course. It's in evidence, and then you will have the procedure and right to examine the object. How about document, is it already --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The document was -- that I've read from is page 16 of P1449 which has been admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I might also point out that we informed the Karadzic Defence that we had this document on the 3rd of March, 2010, we informed them of their right to inspect it pursuant to Rule 66(B). They did exercise that right. And, again, I told them earlier today that we were going to be using this projectile from Markale II, this stabiliser fin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That concludes your evidence, Mr. Higgs. Thank you very much for your coming to give it. Now you're free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will rise, and we will resume at 9.00 tomorrow morning with Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 20th day of August, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.50 p.m.,
